description: Jelastic Cloud (Infomaniak datacenter, Switzerland) — clone-environment-based PROD safety, git-tag-revert DEV. Reference implementation; client code in plugins/shipwright-deploy/scripts/lib/jelastic_client.py.

required_env_vars.name: JELASTIC_TOKEN
required_env_vars.description: Jelastic Personal Access Token for API access (Infomaniak datacenter).

optional_env_vars.name: SUPABASE_ACCESS_TOKEN
optional_env_vars.description: Required only if the project uses Supabase migrations.

rollback.manual_procedure_reference: /shipwright-deploy --rollback (lists backup clones, prompts for confirmation, restores from selected clone)

known_gaps: The DEV git-tag-revert path pins the ref via environment/vcs/rest/editproject and reads it back via environment/vcs/rest/getprojects. Neither endpoint is covered by the Infomaniak reference this profile was written from, so both are documented-not-live-verified. The design is fail-closed: the client raises on any non-zero result, so a wrong endpoint or parameter name is reported as a failed rollback, never as a false success. The first real rollback against a live environment either works or returns a precise API error.
The API token may need broader scope for editproject / getprojects than for vcs/update alone. If a rollback returns an authorization error, widen the token before assuming the endpoint is wrong.

branch=<ref> is how the VCS project carries a ref. Whether a tag or a commit SHA is accepted there (as opposed to a branch name) is unverified against a live environment; the rollback CLI validates ref *shape* only.

Rolling the application back does not roll stored data back. The rollback refuses when migrations exist that the target ref does not know, and names this profile's down-migration strategy — but running the down-migrations remains an operator action.
